# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan: 5 Days for 2 Adults

A balanced Kyoto itinerary for **2026-04-12 to 2026-04-16** with **temples, food markets, one slower day, mid-range hotel near a train station, and public transit only**.
Budget target of **$2,400 total** is very workable; this plan keeps you around **$1,900–$2,250** depending on hotel choice and dining style.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

### Day 1: Arrival + Higashiyama Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Kyoto, check in near **Kyoto Station** or **Shijo/Karasuma** for easy transit.
- Afternoon: Light walk through **Gion** and **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka**; keep it easy after travel.
- Dinner: Simple Kyoto-style meal near the station or in Gion.
- Estimated cost for 2: **Lodging $140–$220 | Food $70–$110 | Transit $10–$20 | Activities $0–$20 | Total $220–$370**

### Day 2: Arashiyama Temples + Riverside
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Head early to **Tenryu-ji** and the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Visit **Iwatayama Monkey Park** or relax along the **Katsura River** area.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/A_Japanese_Macaque_at_Arashiyama_Monkey_Park_Iwatayama%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit **Iwatayama Monkey Park** or relax along the **Katsura River** area, Kyoto, Japan
- Dinner: Tempura, soba, or yudofu in Arashiyama or back near your hotel.
- Estimated cost for 2: **Lodging $140–$220 | Food $80–$120 | Transit $12–$24 | Activities $20–$50 | Total $252–$414**

### Day 3: Fushimi Inari + Nishiki Market
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** early for the best temple-shrine atmosphere and fewer crowds.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/21/Torii_Gates_At_Fushimi_Inari_Taisha_%28129796595%29.jpeg Alt=Morning: Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** early for the best temple-shrine atmosphere and fewer crowds, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Explore **Nishiki Market** for snacks, lunch bites, and Kyoto specialties.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Explore **Nishiki Market** for snacks, lunch bites, and Kyoto specialties, Kyoto, Japan
- Dinner: Casual izakaya or a set meal in central Kyoto.
- Estimated cost for 2: **Lodging $140–$220 | Food $90–$140 | Transit $10–$18 | Activities $0–$20 | Total $240–$398**

### Day 4: Relaxing Day — Philosopher’s Path + Zen Gardens
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Slow start, then visit **Ginkaku-ji** and walk part of the **Philosopher’s Path**.
- Afternoon: Choose one calm stop such as **Nanzen-ji**, **Heian Shrine gardens**, or a tea break.
- Dinner: Comfortable sit-down dinner near downtown Kyoto.
- Estimated cost for 2: **Lodging $140–$220 | Food $80–$130 | Transit $10–$18 | Activities $10–$30 | Total $240–$398**

### Day 5: Kiyomizu-dera + Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Early visit to **Kiyomizu-dera** and nearby temple lanes for final sightseeing.
- Afternoon: Last lunch and souvenir stop, then transfer to Kyoto Station for departure.
- Dinner: Not needed unless your flight is late.
- Estimated cost for 2: **Lodging $140–$220 | Food $50–$90 | Transit $10–$20 | Activities $10–$25 | Total $210–$355**

## Budget Overview for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimated Total | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Lodging | **$700–$1,100** | 4 nights, mid-range hotel near Kyoto Station or Karasuma |
| Food | **$370–$590** | Mix of market food, casual meals, and 1 nicer dinner |
| Transit | **$52–$100** | Mostly subway, JR, and buses; no taxis needed |
| Activities | **$40–$145** | Temple admissions, gardens, optional monkey park |
| Trip Total | **$1,162–$1,935** | Leaves room for upgrades, snacks, and shopping |

## Stay Near Kyoto Station or Karasuma

Best-fit hotel zones for your plan:
- **Kyoto Station area**: easiest for arrivals, departures, and JR/subway access
- **Karasuma/Shijo area**: great central base for food, shopping, and subway connections
- **Recommended room style**: double room or twin room in a 3–4 star business-style hotel
- **What to look for**: breakfast optional, laundry access, 24-hour front desk, and luggage storage

## Packing Checklist for Kyoto in Mid-April

- Light jacket or trench coat
- Layerable tops and a sweater
- Comfortable walking shoes
- Compact umbrella or rain shell
- Socks you can remove easily for temple visits
- Small day bag for transit and market snacks
- Portable phone charger
- Reusable water bottle
- Cash and IC transit card
- Basic meds and blister care
- Sunglasses and sunscreen
- Light scarf for cool mornings/evenings

## Practical Transit Notes

- Use **IC card** transit payments for trains and buses.
- Stay near **Kyoto Station** if you want the simplest airport/train connections.
- For temple-heavy days, start early to avoid the busiest crowds.
- Keep one flexible meal slot each day for market snacks or spontaneous finds.

## Sources

- Kyoto City tourism: https://kyoto.travel/en
- JR West route and station info: https://www.westjr.co.jp/global/en/
- Kyoto municipal subway and bus info: https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/page/0000019958.html
